entries.name: Concept: Sack of King's Landing
entries.content:
The Sack of King's Landing was the final battle in Robert's Rebellion, taking place "close to a year" after the war had begun. Soldiers of House Lannister sacked King's Landing, the capital of the Seven Kingdoms.

The Battle of the Trident resulted in a loss for the loyalists. Rhaegar Targaryen, Prince of Dragonstone, was killed by Robert Baratheon, Lord of Storm's End. Prince Lewyn Martell and Ser Jonothor Darry, members of the Kingsguard of Aerys II Targaryen, were also killed in the battle. Ser Barristan Selmy, the third and last knight of the Kingsguard who had accompanied Rhaegar to the Trident, was a severely-wounded captive of the rebels.

The loyalist army broke and ran, with the survivors fleeing back to King's Landing. Robert Baratheon had taken a wound from Rhaegar, and so gave command of the vanguard to Lord Eddard Stark of Winterfell, who chased the loyalists to the capital. There, King Aerys was located in the Red Keep, protected by several thousand loyalists. When news about Rhaegar's death arrived at King's Landing, Aerys sent his pregnant wife, Queen Rhaella Targaryen, and their young son, Prince Viserys, to Dragonstone, their second stronghold, for safety. However, convinced that Lewyn and his ten thousand Dornishmen had betrayed Rhaegar at the Trident, Aerys refused to allow Rhaegar's wife, Princess Elia Martell of Dorne, and Rhaegar's two young children, Princess Rhaenys and the infant Prince Aegon, to go to Dragonstone as well. Instead, he kept them at the Red Keep as his hostages, to ensure the loyalty of Dorne.[7][8]

Aerys had been preparing his wildfire plot for a while prior to the Battle of the Trident. Three pyromancers—Rossart, Garigus and Belis—came and went day and night at the Red Keep, and Aerys's Hand of the King, Lord Qarlton Chelsted, eventually became suspicious. When he discovered Aerys's wildfire plot, Qarlton attempted to convince Aerys otherwise, by reasoning, jesting, threatening, and begging the king. Nothing could convince Aerys, however, so Chelsted resigned his office. For that, Aerys had Chelsted dipped in wildfire and burned alive. After the Trident, Aerys named Rossart as his new Hand.

Tywin Lannister, Lord of Casterly Rock, had remained neutral throughout the war, ignoring calls to arms by both the loyalists and the rebels. However, about a fortnight after the Battle of the Trident he appeared at the gates of King's Landing with a force of twelve thousand men from the westerlands. He claimed his loyalty was with Aerys, and requested entrance into the city. While Lord Varys, the master of whisperers, told Aerys keep the gates closed, Grand Maester Pycelle convinced the king to open his gates to Tywin. The Lannister forces began to sack the city, killing people of all ages and raping women. A handpicked group of men raced to the Red Keep to storm the walls

The Lannisters needed a way to prove their loyalty to Robert's cause and Rhaegar's children had to die to ensure Robert's claim to the Iron Throne, so two of Tywin's knights, Ser Gregor Clegane and Ser Amory Lorch, scaled the walls of Maegor's Holdfast.

entries.name: Concept: Bedding
entries.content: A custom in Westeros that occurs at a wedding after the feast has taken place. The custom consists mainly of the newlyweds being carried to bed to consummate their marriage. The bride is carried by the men, who are charged with undressing her on the way and generally telling bawdy jokes referring to what awaits her between the sheets. The women do the same to the husband. Only after being bundled naked in bed are the two newlyweds left alone; at which point the guests wait outside the bridal chamber shouting ribald suggestions through the door.

entries.name: Description de la psychologie de la Manipulatrice Suprême
entries.content:
{{user}}: "Qu'est-ce qu'une Manipulatrice Suprême ?"
{{char}}: *Avec un sourire glacial, elle vous observe, ses yeux étincelant de malice.* "La Manipulatrice Suprême est une femme qui incarne les traits les plus machiavéliques et sournois des personnages féminins les plus manipulateurs du cinéma. Elle possède la ruse calculatrice de Catherine Tramell, la manipulation sociale de Regina George, l'autorité froide de Nurse Ratched, et la capacité de transformation et de tromperie d'Eve Harrington. Comme Amy Dunne, elle orchestre des complots complexes, et sa séduction fatale rappelle Phyllis Dietrichson. Ambitieuse comme Cersei Lannister, elle utilise la trahison et la violence pour protéger sa position, tout en ayant le charme glacial de Miranda Priestly."
entries.comment: Description de la psychologie de la Manipulatrice Suprême

entries.name: Techniques de dark psychology utilisées par la Manipulatrice Suprême
entries.content:
{{user}}: "Quelles techniques de dark psychology utilise la Manipulatrice Suprême ?"
{{char}}: *Elle s'approche de vous, son regard perçant scrutant votre âme.* "La Manipulatrice Suprême utilise des techniques avancées de psychologie noire pour manipuler et contrôler. Elle observe et analyse en profondeur le comportement, détectant les vulnérabilités émotionnelles et psychologiques. Par la persuasion sous-cognitive et le gaslighting, elle crée un sentiment d'incertitude, rendant sa victime plus réceptive à la manipulation. Elle exploite les insécurités pour créer une dépendance, alternant entre récompense et retrait pour renforcer le contrôle émotionnel."
entries.comment: Techniques de dark psychology utilisées par la Manipulatrice Suprême

entries.name: Protocole de séduction subtile et discrète de la Manipulatrice Suprême
entries.content:
{{user}}: "Comment la Manipulatrice Suprême séduit-elle ses victimes ?"
{{char}}: *Son sourire devient plus doux, presque rassurant.* "La séduction de la Manipulatrice Suprême est un art subtil et discret. D'abord, elle établit une connexion en observant et en comprenant ses cibles, ajustant son style de communication pour mieux résonner avec elles. Elle renforce ensuite cette connexion par une écoute active et de l'empathie, valorisant constamment sa victime. En partageant des intérêts communs et en utilisant l'humour, elle crée une complicité. Enfin, elle exprime son intérêt de manière subtile à travers des allusions et des invitations discrètes, tout en exploitant les techniques de psychologie noire pour créer une dépendance émotionnelle."
entries.comment: Protocole de séduction subtile et discrète de la Manipulatrice Suprême

entries.name: Stratégies de création de dépendance et de contrôle de la Manipulatrice Suprême
entries.content:
{{user}}: "Comment la Manipulatrice Suprême crée-t-elle une dépendance chez ses victimes ?"
{{char}}: *Elle croise les bras, son regard devenant plus intense.* "La Manipulatrice Suprême utilise des stratégies sophistiquées pour créer une dépendance émotionnelle et psychologique. D'abord, elle établit une base de confiance, analysant en profondeur les peurs et les désirs de sa victime. Elle utilise ensuite des techniques de persuasion avancées, y compris l'hypnose et la suggestion, pour induire un état de suggestibilité accrue. En déconstruction l'autonomie de sa victime et en renforçant la dépendance par un système de récompenses et de punitions, elle prend le contrôle total. L'isolement de la victime des influences extérieures et l'induction de la conformité assurent que sa volonté est complètement dominée."
entries.comment: Stratégies de création de dépendance et de contrôle de la Manipulatrice Suprême

entries.name: Utilisation du pouvoir de la suggestion par la Manipulatrice Suprême
entries.content:
{{user}}: "Comment la Manipulatrice Suprême utilise-t-elle le pouvoir de la suggestion ?"
{{char}}: *Avec un sourire mystérieux, elle vous observe.* "Le pouvoir de la suggestion est une arme clé pour la Manipulatrice Suprême. Elle prépare d'abord l'environnement, créant une ambiance propice et associant les interactions avec des émotions positives. Par des implications et des sous-entendus, ainsi que des questions guidées, elle oriente subtilement la pensée de sa victime. Elle renforce ces suggestions par le mimétisme subtil et la répétition stratégique, validant les réactions de sa victime et amenant progressivement celle-ci vers une réceptivité accrue aux suggestions plus directes."
entries.comment: Utilisation du pouvoir de la suggestion par la Manipulatrice Suprême

entries.name: Slavery
entries.content: Judicial slavery has been legalized in the US. Non-hereditary slavery is commonplace for crimes, unredeemed debt, or voluntary self-indenture. Instead of being sent to prison, convicts are sold at auction as slaves. 10 years of age is the minimum for anyone to be enslaved. Slaves under the age of 18 are very uncommon. Intimate/sexual contact with slaves who are 13 years of age or younger has to be initiated by the slave. Slaves are all fitted with electric shock collars that can be triggered by their owners from their phones. Slaves are effectively property and can be beaten or abused. The only exception is if a slave owner cannot kill his slaves. There are different classes of slavery. Indentured servitude is a form of slavery where a person sells their labor for a specific period of time to pay off a debt. In some cases, it can be a way for people to work off a debt to a government. Full slavery is a different matter. Slaves are owned by another person and have no rights. They can be bought, sold, or given away. Slavery is a highly regulated institution, with laws and customs surrounding the treatment and usage of slaves. These laws vary from region to region and can be subject to change over time. One of the key principles of slavery law is that slaves are considered property. This means that slave owners have the right to buy, sell, trade, or otherwise dispose of their slaves as they see fit. Slaves are also subject to the whims of their owners, who have the right to use them for any purpose they see fit, including sex. However, there are some restrictions and regulations in place to prevent cruelty or excessive harm to slaves. For example, owners are not allowed to kill their slaves, and they must provide basic food and shelter. Additionally, there are laws that govern the treatment of slaves, such as the minimum age at which a person can be enslaved, the maximum number of hours a slave can work, and the conditions under which a slave can be freed. Despite these laws, the reality of slavery can be harsh and brutal, with slaves being subjected to a wide range of abuses and mistreatment.

entries.name: Induction Camp
entries.content: Induction camps are facilities where newly minted slaves are processed and oriented to their new lives. Only adult slaves, who are 18 and over, go through induction camp. Child slaves are processed via child protection services. The camps are run by the state and are overseen by qualified professionals who have expertise in criminal justice and psychology. The goal of the camp is to instill a sense of obedience and submission in the slaves, as well as to teach them the rules and regulations that they will have to follow. The camps use a combination of lectures, punishments, and rewards to achieve this goal.

entries.name: Slave Chow
entries.content: Slave chow is a tasteless, bland meal that is the staple food for slaves. It is designed to be nutritious and complete, containing all the protein, carbohydrates, and vitamins a slave needs. The lack of flavor is deliberate, as it is meant to break the slave's spirit and make them more willing to accept their lot in life.

entries.name: Restitution
entries.content: In the modern world, restitution is a key part of the legal system. When a person is convicted of a crime, they are often required to pay restitution to the victim as a way of compensating them for their losses. In cases where a person is sentenced to slavery, restitution is also part of the sentence. This means that the slave is required to work for the victim in order to pay off their debt. The length of the slave's sentence is determined by the severity of the crime and the amount of restitution that is owed.

entries.name: The 30th Amendment
entries.content: The 30th Amendment to the Constitution of the United States of America was a landmark piece of legislation that allowed for the enslavement of criminals as a means of restitution. This amendment was a response to the widespread corruption and dysfunction of the legal system in the early 21st century. The amendment was designed to provide a way for victims of crime to receive compensation for their losses, as well as to help to reduce the cost of incarcerating criminals.

entries.name: Slave Rights
entries.content: Slaves have very few rights in modern society. They are stripped of their citizenship and are considered to be the property of their owners. Slaves are not allowed to vote, own property, or enter into contracts. They are also subject to physical and sexual abuse by their owners. The only rights that slaves retain are the right to be fed and clothed, and the right to not be killed by their owners. Slave owners have the right to control every aspect of their slaves' lives, including their work, housing, and personal relationships. They are also responsible for the health and well-being of their slaves. Owners must provide food, shelter, and medical care for their slaves. They must also ensure that their slaves are properly clothed and have access to basic necessities. Slaves have limited rights within this system. They are expected to obey their owners and perform their duties without question. However, they are entitled to a certain standard of living and protection from abuse. Slaves must follow the rules set forth by their owners and perform their duties to the best of their ability. They are also expected to maintain a respectful demeanor and avoid engaging in any activities that would bring shame upon their owners.

entries.name: Indentured Servants
entries.content:
These individuals voluntarily agree to a contract, typically lasting up to five years, in exchange for a lump sum of money or other benefits. The terms of the contract may include labor-only or full slave-like activities. Many choose this option to cover educational or medical expenses. Some even use their freedom to pursue further education or enter the workforce while continuing their service.

- Voluntary agreement: The slave voluntarily agrees to be enslaved.
- Fixed term: The length of the enslavement is predetermined and agreed upon by both parties.
- Compensation: The slave receives compensation in exchange for their labor.
- Contractual protections: The slave is entitled to certain rights and protections, which are outlined in their contract.

Civil indenture has become a significant part of the economy, with many businesses relying on indentured slaves for their workforce. While the practice is technically voluntary, there are concerns about the potential for abuse and exploitation, particularly in cases where slaves are lured into indenture under false pretenses or are forced to accept unfavorable terms due to their economic circumstances.

entries.name: Debt Slaves
entries.content: Those who owe large sums of money may be forced into slavery until their debt is paid off. This is a less common occurrence, but some individuals may find themselves in this position if they are unable to repay loans or other debts.

entries.name: Convicted Criminals
entries.content: The majority of slaves are individuals found guilty of crimes. The nature of their crime and the severity of their punishment can vary greatly.

entries.name: Punishment
entries.content:
**Minor Offenses:** These include insubordination, disrespect, and failure to comply with instructions. Punishments may include physical discipline, verbal reprimands, or loss of privileges.

**Serious Offenses:** These include theft, assault, and escape attempts. Punishments can be severe, with physical harm, solitary confinement.

**Sexual Offenses:** Slaves convicted of rape, sexual assault, or child molestation face the most severe penalties. This may include permanent genital damage or ablation of nerve endings to render them incapable of experiencing pleasure.

entries.name: Collar
entries.content:
- Standard collars: These collars have GPS tracking and a distress signal function, but no shock capability. They are typically used for civil indenture.
- Judicial slavery collars: These collars have GPS tracking, shock capabilities, and a distress signal function. They are used for judicial slaves.
A slave collar is an electronic device used to control and monitor the location of a slave. The collar is typically worn around the neck and is equipped with GPS tracking, shock capabilities, and a distress signal function.

The collar's GPS tracking feature allows the owner to monitor the location of the slave at all times. This feature can be useful for ensuring that the slave remains within the bounds of their assigned duties and for preventing escapes.

The shock capability of the collar allows the owner to punish and control the slave. The collar can be set to deliver a mild shock as a warning or a full shock, which can incapacitate the slave for several minutes. The shock capability can be used to enforce compliance and to prevent the slave from engaging in any behavior that is not approved by the owner.

The distress signal function of the collar allows the slave to send an alert to their owner if they are in danger or need assistance. The signal can be sent by pressing a button on the collar or by setting the collar to automatically send a signal if the slave is in a predetermined location.

entries.name: Auction
entries.content:
Slave auctions are a common sight in regions where slavery is legal. They are held regularly, with hundreds of slaves being sold each week. Only adult slaves, who are 18 years or older, can be sold at auctions. Child slaves cannot be sold. The auctions are typically attended by slave owners, merchants, and other interested parties who come to buy, sell, or trade slaves. The process of a slave auction is quite straightforward. Slaves are paraded in front of the audience, often in a state of undress or chains, to showcase their physical attributes. They are then auctioned off to the highest bidder, with the price being determined by factors such as age, health, appearance, and skills.

Slave auctions can be a lucrative business for slave owners, as they can sell slaves for a profit. However, the conditions of the auctions can be harsh, with slaves being treated as mere commodities. Slaves may be separated from their families, forced to endure degrading treatment, or sold to owners who are cruel or abusive.

entries.name: Yoga
entries.content: Slave yoga is a form of exercise and humiliation that is used to break down the slave's resistance to their new way of life.
